revenue from operations stood at INR1,057.84 crores, reflecting growth of 36.53% compared 
with the same quarter of last year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR159.98 crores with an 
EBITDA margin of 15.12%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR81.48 crores.

takes our total solar EPC execution for the H1 FY2027 to 1,345 megawatt peak. Further, our 
order book has strengthened during the quarter with the addition of 1.7 gigawatt peak of new 
orders.

Moving to our unexecuted order book. As of 30th September 2026, our consolidated unexecuted

I also want to highlight the growth in our other revenue segments, which are now meaningfully 
contributing to our revenue. Our operational IPP portfolio stands at 82.82 megawatt peak and 
O&M portfolio has reached to 1.5 gigawatt peak. These businesses strengthen our recurring 
revenue base and help us build long-term relationships with our customers. 
 
Our capability in T&D segment have also continued to strengthen. We are expanding our 
manufacturing capabilities through the additional facility of Azamnagar with a capacity of 1 
lakh metric tons. This further supports our ability to participate in growing requirements for 
transmission and distribution infrastructure. Our capability across EPC of solar, BESS and T&D, 
together with IPP and O&M allows us to participate in a wider part of the energy value chain. 
With this, WRTL is evolving from a pure solar EPC player into a broader energy transition EPC 
platform. 
 
Let me now turn to the broader industry environment, where momentum across India's 
renewable energy sector remains strong, especially in solar. As of 30th September 2026, India's 
installed renewable energy capacity stood at around 299 gigawatt. The solar has contributed 
around 171 gigawatt. Within solar itself, ground-mounted projects contributed more than 125 
gigawatt; grid-connected rooftops around 33 gigawatt; and hybrid and off-grid together around 
12 gigawatt. 
 
The government has also recently approved the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, which targets 5 
gigawatts of floating solar with co-located energy storage of at least 2 hours. With this, further 
enhanced the segment of floating solar and energy storage. As solar become a larger part of the 
grid, battery storage is becoming essential to deliver that power when it is needed. The CEA 
estimates India's battery storage requirement at  around 208 gigawatt hours by 2030, and the 
project pipeline is building up with this. 
 
As of May 2026, the BESS projects above 1 megawatt hour stands at around 144 gigawatt hours, 
of which around 7.5 gigawatt hours already commissioned, another 42 gigawatt hours under 
construction and 39 gigawatt hours has been awarded and another 55 gigawatts on tender stage. 
And this clearly highlights the demand towards BESS is growing in the country, which is a clear 
opportunity for the company to offer solar and BESS EPC solution. 
 
Furthermore, the Union Cabinet recently approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 scheme 
with a total outlay of around INR1.86 lakh crores. The scheme aims to strengthen intrastate 
transmission infrastructure for the evacuation of up to 135 gigawatt of renewable energy and the 
deployment of 50 gigawatt hours of battery energy storage by FY 2032 and 33. 
 
This highlights the growing requirement of renewable, BESS and stronger T&D network to meet 
the demand of growing electricity through non-fossil fuel. We see a strong opportunity to
